title: When is an estimate especially limited?
statement:
Why can an average C–H bond enthalpy differ from the exact value for a specific bond?

[_]{a}

choices: Bond strength depends on the molecular environment.
Every C–H bond always has the same energy.
C–H bonds cannot break in the gas phase.
The result depends only on C’s atomic number.
explanations: Average entries need not equal a molecule-specific dissociation enthalpy.
This is the assumption the average cannot guarantee.
Connectivity and molecular environment also matter.

hints: C–H bonds can occur in different molecular surroundings.
Different environments can alter the dissociation energy.
solution: Define the entries as averages. C–H bonds can occur in different molecular surroundings. Different environments can alter the dissociation energy. Average entries need not equal a molecule-specific dissociation enthalpy.
